title: Integration throttle check-in: NimbusHealth onramp (standup digest)
content:
Meeting: SE + ProServices weekly sync — NimbusHealth Onramp
Date: 2026-09-09 10:00 PT (30m) — standup style
Attendees: Asha (lead), Marcus (field eng), Diego (infra), Priya (solutions eng), Samira (customer success), Rahul (Nimbus SRE via phone)
Context: Customer load test yesterday exposed request-throttling edge behavior at peak simulated traffic for search/relevance rerank pipeline. They are on Dedicated pilot (2xA100 reserved) and hitting transient 503s when KV cache misses spike. Goal: triage root cause, short-term mitigation to keep SLAs, and long-term runtime tuning plan.

Quick summary:
- Incident observed: 503s at 18:35 PT during a 10k qps synthetic run; error rate ~1.8% over 10m window. Correlated with an increase in tail sequence lengths and simultaneous model reloads triggered by small config drift.
- Immediate hypothesis: competing CPU work (model reload + trace collection) contended on control-plane tasks causing request routing delays and throttler decisions.
- Short-term mitigation already applied by Diego: paused non-essential debug trace collection on Dedicated nodes and increased per-tenant token-concurrency soft limit from 80 -> 120 for Nimbus test pool (controlled burst). Error rate dropped to 0.15% in a 15m follow-up run.

Notes / deep-dive snippets:
- Logs we looked at: node-ctl logs show repeated kernel scheduling waits around model-serializer step; redis latency spikes for prefix-cache during same interval.
- Diego: observed GC compaction spikes in inference-proxy at 18:34; those coincide with a policy evaluator spin. Need to validate if config rollout triggered evaluator loops.
- Marcus: customer-side pattern — they sent longer conversational contexts from the staging UI due to a recent client-side change. This increased KV cache misses by ~22%.
- Priya: suggested enabling sticky routing to warm nodes for high-affinity customers during ramp windows; trade-off: less global pooling, potentially lower avg utilization.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Diego: produce a micro-run reproducer (script + dataset) that recreates the 503 pattern and capture perf profile (deadline 2026-09-13). LINK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/nimbus-integrations/pull/78 (WIP).
- Priya: prototype sticky-routing override in the canary control plane and run A/B against normal routing for the next scheduled soak test (deadline 2026-09-16).
- Marcus: ask Nimbus SRE to throttle staging client side to cap context length to 1.5k tokens until we have warm-nodes in place; confirm by 2026-09-10.
- Asha: schedule a 60m triage on 2026-09-12 with infra (diego), runtime (sam), and Nimbus SRE to validate model reload triggers and policy-evaluator behavior.
- Samira: update the customer success playbook with the short-term workaround and customer messaging draft (ETA 2026-09-11).

Open blockers / questions:
- Why did config drift cause multiple model reloads at once? (Diego suspects a CI/CD hook retrigger; need env audit).
- Is the per-tenant soft limit bump safe across other tenants on the same pool? (capacity team to confirm).
- Should we enable sticky routing by default for Dedicated pilots? Ops impact unknown.

Temporary risk register (quick):
- Risk: manual soft-limit increase could starve other tenants during multi-tenant bursts. Mitigation: apply only to customer-specific pool and monitor.
- Risk: sticky routing may reduce efficiency, increasing per-token cost by estimated +8–12%. Will model in Optimize next sprint.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Apply short-term soft-limit increase to Nimbus dedicated pool (rolled back after validation window).
- Pause debug trace collection on dedicated nodes until confirmed safe to re-enable.

Notes to self / informal:
- Priya note: follow up with runtime team about making model reloads idempotent w.r.t. policy-evaluator triggers — might be a quick fix (low-risk) if we guard reload on config fingerprint.
- Marcus note: Nimbus is sensitive to UX latency; CS wants a one-paragraph customer-friendly explanation that avoids platform jargon. Samira will draft.
- Diego TODO: check k8s job that runs nightly config-sync for Dedicated pools — maybe it retried at 18:30 due to transient api failure.

Next meeting cadence: weekly sync continues; schedule additional triage (2026-09-12 11:00 PT).

Appendix (quick logs / refs):
- Repro notes (short): run loadtool --profile nimbus-long-context --concurrency 9000 --duration 10m, attach perf dump on node-ctl.
- Related tickets: PROJ-4321 (customer-throttle-investigation), INFRA-981 (diagnose-nightly-config-sync).
- Slack threads: #se-nimbus-onramp (pinned logs)

End of notes.

-- Asha
